note: The only published point for the buried temple is the Wikidata/Polish Wikipedia one (35°51'15"N 14°27'56"E, one source family); MaltaToday locates id-Debdieba only in words ('on the road to Hal Farrug', 450 m south-west of the 2007 Lufthansa Technik hangar), and the stored point sits on Luqa village. No second independent source prints coordinates, so the point is held for the owner.

The site is the univallate hillfort at the northern end of Creech Hill, scheduled as 'Hillfort at Fox Covert, 550m north east of Lamyatt Lodge' (NHLE 1016303) at ST 66610 36648, which is about 51.128, -2.4785 and roughly 1.2 km NW of the stored point. Only Wikidata prints that point in latitude and longitude. The Somerset HER (ST 6665 3677), the aubreyresearch copy of the NHLE entry and the 1957 UBSS note give grid references only, and the Atlas of Hillforts and The Modern Antiquarian cannot be read without a script or are refused, so no second independent latitude/longitude can be quoted.

The petroglyph rock stands on the right bank of the Queros River near Pillcopata, Kosnipata, at 825 m (Hostnig). The Wikidata/Wikipedia point matches the hamlet Comunidad Nativa Queros Wachiperi, not the rock, and only one source (an OpenStreetMap node 'Petroglifo de Hinkiori' at about -12.934, -71.381) gives the rock itself. The stored point lies about 48 km away in the highlands. With no two independent sources for the site's point, it is held for the owner.

The Tomb of the Birds is tomb NC 2 in the north cliff of Giza's far Western Cemetery. Only OpenStreetMap (shown through Mapcarta, which prints latitude and longitude separately with DMS in between) places it at about 29.979, 31.125. Digital Giza, Andrew Collins and other pages describe its position only in words, so no two independent sources give a quotable point.

The site is a cropmark enclosure (a possible Roman marching camp) on Jaw Hill near Kirkhamgate; the only point printed anywhere is the hill's own point in its Wikipedia article (53.7057, -1.5573), mirrored by copies of that article, and no independent source gives the enclosure's point.

The entry is a region, the archaeological landscape of the lower Swat valley between Chakdara and Saidu Sharif, not one site; its own Wikidata item (Q6693857) carries no coordinates and the linked item Q139570137 gives the centre of the whole Swat Valley (45 km off). No two sources give a point for the site itself, so the point is held for the owner.

The church is Ayazini Kilisesi (Meryem Ana / Oyma Kilise) at the village entrance; the only printed points for it are the OpenStreetMap node 'Ayazini Kilisesi' (39.0106270, 30.5650790, tagged 'source estimated') and the Wikidata group item 'Churches in Ayazini Metropolis', which repeats that point's longitude and is not independent, while Kültür Envanteri places the church about 200 m further east without printing the point. The Wikidata/Wikipedia point of the village (0.96 km away) is not the site.

The only source placing this structure ('Apollonia Yapı Kalıntısı', Kaş) is the Kültür Envanteri entry, whose point Wikidata Q135582527 copies (P11729); no second independent source gives the site's point. The ancient city of Apollonia itself lies about 4 km to the NE (Pleiades 36.186, 29.764), so the city's coordinates cannot stand in for it.

The Devil's Causeway is an 89 km Roman road that leaves Dere Street near Portgate, north of Corbridge, and runs to Berwick-upon-Tweed. The stored point is in Corbridge village itself, south of the road's start, so it is not on the road. The only latitude/longitude found is Wikidata's mid-route point (55.308, -1.809), which the Italian Wikipedia repeats from the same family. The Keys to the Past record N12394, Roman-Britain.co.uk and Co-Curate print no coordinates, so no two independent sources give a point for the road.

Watling Street is a Roman road of several hundred kilometres from Dover and Richborough through London and St Albans to Wroxeter; the English Wikipedia article prints no coordinates for it, and Wikidata's point lies at Canterbury, 89 km from the stored point in Camden, which is not on the road's line (Edgware Road). No two independent sources give one point for the road as a whole, so the point is held for the owner.

Only the Wikimedia family gives a point for the villa: the Wikidata item 'Bradford-on-Avon Roman Villa' (NHLE 1493272) at 51.351994, -2.262604, about 0.25 km from the stored point, and the school's Wikipedia coordinates. The Historic England entry cannot be read, and no second independent readable source prints the villa's coordinates (other pages give only the grid reference ST 817615).

The site is the Çatalat (Çatlar) ruins in the Tektek mountains, 16 km south-east of Soğmatar in Engelli (Küneftar) village, Viranşehir district. The linked Wikidata item and Wikipedia article are the district town Viranşehir, about 36 km away, which is not this site. OpenStreetMap's Çatlar hamlet lies about 0.13 km from the stored point, but no page prints coordinates for the ruins, so there are not two quotable sources for the site's point.

Wikipedia (and Wikidata and GeoNames 3587680) give only the rounded 17°30′N 89°24′W, 2.6 km from the stored point; the one precise gazetteer point (GeoNames 11374359 via Mapcarta, 17.53188, -89.31268) lies 9.6 km east and is printed in a form no quote can hold; no two independent sources give a quotable precise point, so the point is held for the owner.

The site is Ezida, the Nabu temple on the Nimrud acropolis. Vici.org places it at 36.097092, 43.330299, next to the stored point, but no second independent readable source prints the temple's own coordinates (Pleiades' Ezida record is behind a bot challenge; other pages give only Nimrud as a whole), so the point is held for the owner.
